summary: BA's 'JSONL pruned' finding is factually wrong — investigation was incomplete; two strong candidate JSONLs exist in /root/.claude/projects/-root/ from 2026-04-21 17:07 and 18:04 UTC bracketing b5d447e's 17:45 UTC author time, and both grep-match the commit's distinctive tokens (sync uncommitted, b5d447e, merge-overnight). BA pre-declared a fallback that dev would now write into the postmortem as a falsehood, violating R5 spec criterion.

objections.claim: BA spec lines 38, 78, 138, 154, 180; context JSON line 143; AC9: 'Session transcript is pruned' / 'JSONL pruned' / `/root/.claude/projects/-dev-shm-dev-workspace-dot-claude/` only spans 2026-04-15 to 2026-04-16 / 'Recovering 2026-04-21 session JSONL — verified pruned by BA'.
objections.problem: BA searched ONE project directory (`-dev-shm-dev-workspace-dot-claude`) and prematurely concluded the JSONL is pruned. Direct verification by QA shows: (a) `/root/.claude/projects/-root/` contains 8 JSONLs modified on 2026-04-21, including `05dd71c2-...jsonl` at 17:07:32 UTC (~38 min BEFORE b5d447e commit 17:45:03 UTC) and `962de59f-...jsonl` at 18:04:31 UTC (~19 min AFTER b5d447e), bracketing the commit time; (b) `grep -l 'sync.*uncommitted|b5d447e|merge-overnight'` against both candidates MATCHES both files. The JSONL very likely exists in `-root/` (b5d447e was committed during a session whose CWD was `/root` or `/root/.claude/`, hence the project mapping `-root`). BA's pre-declaration of `JSONL pruned` would cause dev to write a falsehood into the postmortem, which (i) violates spec 5.2.5 R5 requirement that the User-prompt-recovered section TRUTHFULLY identify a JSONL path OR truthfully declare pruned; (ii) contradicts the user's standing memory entry `feedback_qa_spec_alignment.md` ('Never claim PASS without evidence'); (iii) contradicts the user's literal complaint in spec 5.1 about wanting the regression understood, not papered over.
objections.required_evidence: BA must (a) re-run the JSONL search across ALL `/root/.claude/projects/*/` directories with date window 2026-04-21 16:00 UTC to 2026-04-21 19:00 UTC and report all candidates; (b) for each candidate, grep for distinctive tokens from the b5d447e commit message ('sync all uncommitted', 'merge-overnight', 'runcode-watchdog', 'install-checkpoint-refspec', etc.) and report match counts; (c) only if NO candidate shows any match across ALL directories may BA declare pruned. The current spec's literal string `JSONL pruned` directive must be REMOVED and replaced with 'dev MUST identify the actual session JSONL path' — the candidates `-root/05dd71c2-...jsonl` and `-root/962de59f-...jsonl` are the starting points.

objections.claim: BA spec Constraints/dev_constraint at line 78 + context JSON line 143: 'the `## User-prompt-recovered` section MUST contain the literal string `JSONL pruned` (case-insensitive). Spec 5.2.5 explicitly authorizes this fallback at line 251.'
objections.problem: Spec 5.2.5 line 251 authorizes `JSONL pruned` as a FALLBACK only when JSONL has actually been pruned. BA inverted this — turning a conditional fallback into a MANDATE that dev must write that literal regardless of whether the JSONL exists. The investigation Section 5.2.5 prescribes (questions 1-4 about user prompt, hook warnings, refactor intent, contract surfacing) was entirely OUTSOURCED to dev as a TODO. BA's only investigation deliverable was a single `ls` of one project directory. The user's spec language 'investigate why the problem occurred' (line 240) requires actual analysis, not a one-line directory listing. Worse, the b5d447e commit message itself contains substantial evidence BA didn't analyze (`Generated with [Claude Code]` + `Co-Authored-By: Claude` + `via [Happy]` — proves AI-authored; 93 files including 4 specific hook rewrites named in the body — proves the rewrite was deliberate, not accidental). BA never even quoted the commit body.
objections.required_evidence: BA must re-do the investigation step itself: (a) read at least one of the candidate JSONLs from `-root/` and quote the user's actual prompt that led to b5d447e; (b) analyze the b5d447e commit body's listed file changes for evidence of intent (was `posttool-git-checkpoint.sh` rewrite explicitly requested or a side-effect?); (c) check git reflog / event log for any pre-commit hook firings around 2026-04-21 17:45 UTC. Only after BA has done its own investigation can it tell dev what to write in the postmortem's User-prompt-recovered and Agent-reasoning sections. As written, BA is asking dev to manufacture a fictional postmortem.

objections.claim: BA spec Affected files / context JSON parallel_groups: BOTH project repo (`/dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/`) AND global config (`/root/.claude/`) are in scope per spec 5.3.1, but BA's parallel_groups specify edits ONLY to `/root/.claude/commands/*` (G1, G2, G3) and `/root/.claude/hooks/*` (G4), justifying this with: 'verified that project repo has no `.claude/commands/` directory of its own (only the global path is authoritative)'.
objections.problem: QA verified `/dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/.claude/` contains `hooks/`, `dev-registry/`, `INDEX.md`, `settings.json`, and overnight-state files but NOT `commands/`. So BA's claim about commands/ absence is correct. HOWEVER — spec 5.3.1 lines 269-274 explicitly lists `.claude/hooks/` (e.g., pretool-overnight-hook-guard.py) under the project repo as an in-scope authoritative target. The project repo DOES have `.claude/hooks/` (verified by `ls`). BA's parallel_groups edits ONLY `/root/.claude/hooks/pretool-overnight-hook-guard.py` and never asks dev to investigate whether the project repo's `.claude/hooks/` contains its own (potentially divergent) copy of `pretool-overnight-hook-guard.py`, or whether the project repo's hooks dir is a symlink, or whether harness ever loads from there. Without this clarification, dev may make changes that are silently shadowed at runtime. Additionally, BA's claim merge.md is '143 lines' is off by one (actual: 142); hook is '482 lines' off by one (actual: 481). Minor but reflects sloppy direct-measurement.
objections.required_evidence: BA must (a) verify whether `/dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/.claude/hooks/` contains a divergent copy of `pretool-overnight-hook-guard.py` or is otherwise consulted by the harness, and document the relationship; (b) if a project-repo copy exists, decide whether it must also be edited (R4.1) or whether the global is canonical; (c) correct line-count statements (merge.md=142, hook=481) so downstream dev does not waste cycles chasing off-by-one anchors.

objections.claim: BA spec Should Have / Constraints: 'settings.json edits are the user's domain per global CLAUDE.md ... dev should produce the proposed JSON additions in the dev-report and explicitly leave registration to the user' (BA spec line 142, 322; context JSON 'should-have' in G4 task list).
objections.problem: BA correctly identifies that settings.json registration is required for the 3 new hooks (R4.2/R4.3/R4.4) to actually fire. However, BA classifies this as Should-Have / 'leave to user'. Spec Section 5.2.4 acceptance criteria for R4 (lines 232-234) require functional verification: 'a Claude Code session that attempts `git commit` outside the blessed bridge gets blocked by `pretool-git-privilege-guard.py` ... exit code 2 with stderr containing `BLOCKED: agent git commit`'. An UNREGISTERED hook will never block anything. Therefore registration is implicitly Must-Have for the spec's verification signals to pass. BA has effectively created a path where dev produces 4 hook files that all pass file-existence checks but where none actually fire — the b5d447e-class regression remains UN-guarded after Cycle 2 'completes'. This is a scope-shrinkage anti-pattern that the user's memory (`feedback_qa_spec_alignment.md`) explicitly forbids.
objections.required_evidence: BA must either (a) escalate settings.json registration to Must-Have and propose a concrete mechanism (update-config skill, or a one-shot user instruction at the top of the dev report), AND adjust the AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8 verification approach to test the hook actually fires (not just that the file exists); OR (b) acknowledge that without registration, R4 verification signals are not achievable in this cycle and explicitly mark R4 as deferred — but this contradicts the cycle's stated scope. Pretending registration is Should-Have while the spec's verification signal requires the hook to actually block is the hidden defect.

objections.claim: BA spec line 38 + context JSON line 444: 'project repo HEAD `0ba2ddfc feat: cycle 1 (14 pipelines) + close-remediation`'.
objections.problem: QA verified project repo HEAD is actually `1128992c checkpoint: Auto-save at 2026-04-25 12:40:32` — there are 4+ checkpoint commits AFTER 0ba2ddfc, plus a real semantic commit `4381eaf5 feat: cycle 2 (codex protocol activation) + close-remediation` between them. The codex-protocol-activation commit (4381eaf5) is likely a SIBLING engineering effort that may or may not interact with this cycle's R1-R5 work (e.g., it may have already touched hook files or commands). BA's stale snapshot creates a risk that dev's parallel work conflicts with already-landed work from a sibling cycle.
objections.required_evidence: BA must re-read the current `git log -5` of both repos and document any commits since BA originally captured HEAD that touched files in BA's modify/create lists. If 4381eaf5 (cycle 2 codex protocol activation) modified any of: merge.md / dev-overnight.md / spec.md / pretool-overnight-hook-guard.py / settings.json, BA must reconcile or explicitly document non-overlap before dispatch.
